candidates.label: Macedonia (Roman province, using Thessalonica, its capital, as label point)
candidates.support: Macedonia's Wikidata item for the Roman province carries no coordinate of its own, so this point is Wikidata's coordinate for Thessalonica, the province's capital throughout the Roman period; it sits about 1.5 km from this project's own 'thessalonica' record, a reasonable margin for a province-level label built from a capital-city point.

summary.text: Macedonia was the Roman province covering northern Greece, with its capital at Thessalonica. Acts describes Paul receiving a night vision of 'a man of Macedonia' begging him to come and help, after which he founded churches at Philippi, Thessalonica and Berea, all cities of this province; several of Paul's letters are addressed to or mention believers there.

history.text: Macedonia became a Roman province in 146 BC, after Rome's final defeat of the Macedonian kingdom, with its capital at Thessalonica and a governor of proconsular rank.

Until AD 15, and again from AD 44 onward, Macedonia was a senatorial province governed by a proconsul; in between, Tiberius placed it under an imperial procurator jointly with Achaia. The senatorial arrangement that Claudius restored in AD 44 was still in force at AD 50.

scripture.textWEB: A vision appeared to Paul in the night. There was a man of Macedonia standing, begging him and saying, “Come over into Macedonia and help us.”
and from there to Philippi, which is a city of Macedonia, the foremost of the district, a Roman colony. We were staying some days in this city.
You yourselves also know, you Philippians, that in the beginning of the Good News, when I departed from Macedonia, no assembly shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving but you only.
so that you became an example to all who believe in Macedonia and in Achaia.
